documents.text: [PAGE 1] Cooperative Law RAG — Book Chapter Structure | Page 1 Book Chapter Structure Adaptive, Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Cooperative Law: A Trustworthy Legal Question Answering Framework 1. Introduction • Background of AI in legal information retrieval • Challenges in understanding Cooperative Law • Limitations of conventional keyword-based legal search • Limitations of conventional RAG for legal question answering • Need for adaptive, explainable, and uncertainty-aware legal RAG • Motivation for applying RAG to Cooperative Law • Objectives and contributions of the proposed framework • Organization of the chapter 2.

Cooperative Law and Legal Question Answering 2.1 Overview of Cooperative Law • Cooperative societies and their legal framework • Acts, rules, regulations, and related legal documents 2.2 Challenges in Cooperative-Law Question Answering • Large legal documents • Section/subsection dependencies • Legal terminology • Questions requiring multiple provisions • Ambiguous or complex questions • Risk of unsupported legal answers 2.3 Need for Evidence-Grounded Legal AI • Importance of retrieving the correct legal provisions • Need for source-based answers • Need to communicate uncertainty 3.

Background and Related Technologies 3.1 Retrieval-Augmented Generation • Basic RAG architecture: retrieval → context → generation 3.2 Dense Retrieval • Semantic embeddings and meaning-based retrieval 3.3 Sparse/BM25 Retrieval [PAGE 2] Cooperative Law RAG — Book Chapter Structure | Page 2 • Keyword-based retrieval and exact legal terminology 3.4 Hybrid Retrieval • Combining dense and BM25 retrieval 3.5 Reciprocal Rank Fusion • Combining multiple ranked retrieval results 3.6 Cross-Encoder Reranking • Refining the relevance ranking of retrieved legal passages 3.7 Explainable and Uncertainty-Aware RAG • Retrieval confidence, evidence explanation, self-critique, and abstention 4.

Proposed Adaptive and Explainable Legal RAG Framework 4.1 Overall Architecture Legal Documents → Preprocessing → Hierarchy-Aware Chunking → Embeddings/ChromaDB → User Query → Query Rewriting → Complexity Detection → Adaptive Routing → Hybrid Retrieval → RRF → Reranking → Confidence Assessment → LLM Generation → Self-Critique → Unified Trust Score → Uncertainty-Aware Answer 4.2 Legal Document Ingestion and Preprocessing • PDF upload, text validation, extraction, cleaning, and document preparation 4.3 Hierarchy-Aware Legal Chunking • Preserve Act → Section → Subsection → Legal provision relationships where appropriate 4.4 Vector Representation and Knowledge Storage • Embedding generation, vector storage, ChromaDB, and section/subsection metadata 4.5 Query Rewriting • Reformulation of the original user question to improve legal retrieval 4.6 Query Complexity Detection and Adaptive Routing • MEDIUM → one retrieval round • HARD → iterative search → evidence check → follow-up query → search again 4.7 Hybrid Legal Retrieval • Dense semantic retrieval and BM25 keyword retrieval in parallel 4.8 Reciprocal Rank Fusion • Combine dense and BM25 ranked lists 4.9 Cross-Encoder Reranking • Re-score and reorder retrieved legal passages 5.

Retrieval Confidence and Adaptive Evidence Assessment 5.1 Retrieval Confidence Score • Top retrieval score, score gap, and average top-result scores [PAGE 3] Cooperative Law RAG — Book Chapter Structure | Page 3 5.2 Relevant and Confident Decision • Low confidence → reformulate/retry or report insufficient confidence • Sufficient confidence → continue to generation 5.3 Why Confidence Matters in Cooperative Law • Reduce the risk of presenting apparently authoritative answers with insufficient evidence 6. Explainable Legal Evidence Retrieval 6.1 Need for Explainability • Show which legal chunks were used and how strongly they contributed 6.2 Retrieval Explainability Heatmap • Dense retrieval score • BM25 score • Cross-encoder reranking score • Final retrieval weight 6.3 Interpretation of Evidence • Help users understand why particular legal provisions were considered relevant 7.

Grounded Legal Answer Generation 7.1 Context Construction • Select high-quality retrieved chunks and provide them to the LLM 7.2 LLM-Based Answer Generation • Generate answers using retrieved legal evidence 7.3 Evidence-Based Legal Responses • Keep answers tied to retrieved cooperative-law provisions 8. Generation Self-Critique and Uncertainty-Aware Answering 8.1 Generation Self-Critique • Second AI pass evaluates each answer sentence against source chunks • Grounded / Weakly Supported / Unsupported 8.2 Unified Abstention Decision • Combine retrieval confidence and generation self-critique into a final trust score • Show the answer or flag it as uncertain 8.3 Uncertainty-Aware Answer Highlighting • Green = grounded; Yellow = weakly supported; Red = unsupported • Display highlighting alongside the retrieval heatmap 9.

System Implementation [PAGE 4] Cooperative Law RAG — Book Chapter Structure | Page 4 9.1 Technology Stack • Python, PyMuPDF, embedding model, ChromaDB, BM25, RRF, Cross-Encoder, LLM, Streamlit/frontend 9.2 System Architecture • Offline document processing and query-time processing 9.3 User Interface • PDF upload, question input, retrieved evidence, heatmap, final answer, uncertainty highlighting 10. Experimental Evaluation 10.1 Dataset • Cooperative-law documents, sections, document types, and question-answer dataset 10.2 Evaluation Questions • Simple, section-specific, multi-section, complex, and ambiguous questions 10.3 Retrieval Evaluation • Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR, NDCG 10.4 Answer Evaluation • Correctness, groundedness/faithfulness, evidence accuracy, unsupported statement rate 10.5 Uncertainty Evaluation • Correct identification of confident, weak-evidence, unsupported, and abstention cases 11.

Ablation and Comparative Analysis • Basic RAG • Hybrid RAG • Hybrid + Reranking • Adaptive Hybrid RAG • Adaptive + Self-Critique • Complete Proposed Framework • Ablations: query rewriting, BM25, dense retrieval, RRF, reranking, adaptive routing, self-critique, abstention 12. Discussion 12.1 Advantages • Better handling of complex legal questions, evidence transparency, and identification of uncertain answers 12.2 Limitations • Document quality, embedding limitations, LLM limitations, threshold sensitivity, legal interpretation, and possible false confidence 12.3 Practical Applicability to Cooperative Law • Potential use by students, researchers, cooperative-society members, legal professionals, administrators, and policy researchers [PAGE 5] Cooperative Law RAG — Book Chapter Structure | Page 5 13.

Future Scope • Multilingual Cooperative Law RAG • Hindi/English legal question answering • Case-law integration • Temporal/version-aware legislation • Citation verification • Knowledge graphs • Improved legal reasoning and human-in-the-loop verification • Improved calibrated uncertainty and cross-document legal relationship analysis 14. Conclusion Cooperative-law documents → Hierarchy-aware preprocessing → Adaptive query processing → Hybrid retrieval → RRF → Cross-encoder reranking → Retrieval confidence → Explainable heatmap → Evidence-grounded generation → Sentence-level self-critique → Unified trust/abstention → Uncertainty-aware legal answer
